item.title: This new Times Square hotel will have a free-fall thrill ride, an observation deck and a rooftop pool
item.description: New York City’s most iconic address is getting a 1,800-key hotel, bringing with it plenty more reasons to visit.

item.title: Nature recovery is falling behind. Can COP17 get global action back on track?
item.description: Biodiversity goals are off track as the UN nature summit faces funding and political tensions on its final day.

item.title: North Korea warns South Korea with ballistic missiles as Seoul calls for talks to ease border tensions
item.description: Missile launches and a dispute over a landmine incident have heightened tensions between the two Koreas. Seoul is seeking military talks to prevent accidental clashes, but Pyongyang has yet to respond.

item.title: Italy inflation surges to 5.4% in October as energy costs bite
item.description: Italian inflation rose 5.4% in October from a year earlier, a sharp rise from the 4.2% rate in September, Italy's statistics agency Istat said on Friday.

item.title: AstraZeneca profit jumps 23% on cancer drugs as it unveils major savings plan
item.description: AstraZeneca's net profit jumped 23% in the third quarter on booming sales of its cancer drugs, as the British drugmaker unveiled a programme to save $1.5 billion (€1.34bn) a year to invest back into developing new medicines.

item.title: China rejects report of spy plot targeting Nvidia's Jensen Huang
item.description: "Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information - not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets - and zero information relevant to national security," a spokesperson for Nvidia told the AFP news agency on Friday.

item.title: EU deforestation law faces enforcement test as palm oil giants risk violations
item.description: After several setbacks, the EU's anti-deforestation rules are due to take force on 30 December 2026.

item.title: How the Binance hack happened and who was behind it
item.description: Investigators say several factors may have been involved, including a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, with signs pointing to North Korean actors being responsible.

item.title: ‘Removing Netanyahu is the most important thing’, Mustafa Barghouti tells Euronews
item.description: Changing the government in Israel is the top priority for Palestinians, according to one of the West Bank’s most prominent political figures. Arab parties hold the balance of power after Israel’s election and would be key to forming a new government.

item.title: Ukraine holds its breath as humanitarian operation begins in Russian-occupied Oleshky
item.description: After years of Russian occupation, civilians in Oleshky face a rare chance to receive humanitarian aid or escape the town, but serious concerns remain over whether those seeking evacuation will be allowed to reach Ukrainian-controlled territory.

item.title: Indonesia: nine orangutans rescued from wildfires return to the forest
item.description: Nine orangutans rescued from devastating wildfires in Indonesian Borneo have returned to the forest after weeks of rehabilitation. Among them are four mothers with their young, including three females expecting another baby.

item.title: Bilbao, Wrocław and Bordeaux top the best-value destinations list for 2027
item.description: You could save up to two-thirds on flight prices and hotel stays by selecting the right city for your next holiday.

item.title: BP profit quadruples as Iran war sends refining margins soaring and debt tumbles
item.description: BP's net profit quadrupled between July and September as the Iran war sent refining margins and oil prices soaring, with the British energy giant beating forecasts and cutting its net debt by $8.4 billion (€7.5bn) ahead of a strategy update in December.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 30th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 30th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Apple Pay and Google Pay launch in Uzbekistan amid wider fintech reforms
item.description: The rollout follows changes to personal data laws and high-level talks with Google. The Central Bank tells Euronews that work is underway to include domestic payment networks Uzcard and HUMO.

item.title: Cameroonian families call for repatriation of relatives sent to fight for Russia in Ukraine
item.description: Lured by the promise of employment in Russia, young Cameroonian men have instead found themselves thrust onto the front lines in Ukraine.

item.title: Which vaccinations should you have this autumn and which are recommended in Germany
item.description: In Germany new recommendations for coronavirus vaccinations now apply. Even last year far fewer people had themselves vaccinated against flu.

item.title: EU countries pledge 20.5mn diesel barrels as winter supply fears grow
item.description: The eleven countries also urged Brussels to ensure the bloc has functioning refineries capable of turning crude oil into the products its economy consumes, like diesel or jet fuel.

item.title: US: flowers laid at Patrick Stewart's Hollywood star after his death
item.description: Flowers have been placed at Patrick Stewart's Hollywood Walk of Fame star following reports of the British actor's death at 86. Visitors gather in Los Angeles to remember his celebrated screen roles.

item.title: Naples Airport to close for the whole of November for €30m revamp – here’s what passengers need to know
item.description: The Italian airport will shut for the entire month of November for major runway upgrades, with flights diverted to nearby Salerno and extra bus and taxi services planned to limit disruption.

item.title: French presidential candidate Édouard Philippe designated 'assisted witness' in embezzlement case
item.description: Through his lawyer, Philippe welcomed the decision to have been given assisted witness status, which is less serious than being formally investigated. "This confirms that there is nothing to reproach him for in this case," his lawyer told the AFP news agency.

item.title: 'You look like hell': Trump berates reporter who asks if he is tired of campaigning
item.description: US President Donald Trump berated a Reuters reporter who questioned whether he had cancelled a planned Kansas rally because he was tired of campaigning ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: US: Trump hands out sweets as Air Force One soars overhead
item.description: Donald and Melania Trump welcomed children in Halloween costumes to the White House on Thursday. The couple handed out sweets, posed for photographs and watched Air Force One fly overhead.

item.title: Tech firms take fresh hit as disappointing earnings fan AI fears
item.description: Tech firms were again on the back foot on Friday after another round of disappointing earnings from Wall Street titans, fanned already by deep concerns about the AI investment boom.

item.title: Halloween in Portugal: from Pão por Deus to Goat and Canhoto, how Portugal celebrates Witches' Day
item.description: Carved pumpkins, sinister masks and children knocking on doors. Besides Halloween, "Pão por Deus" survives: in Portugal these are two ways to mark the year's scariest time.

item.title: 2026 science Nobel Prizes: Who are the winners, and is there a gender gap problem? | Password
item.description: Password is Euronews Tech Talks’ new monthly series unpacking tech and health tech news from Europe and the world. In this first episode, we discover who the scientists awarded Nobel Prizes are, and whether the award has a gender gap issue.

item.title: Drone attack and fire reported at Russia's Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery
item.description: According to Rosneft, the Novokuibyshevsk refinery can process around 8.8 million tonnes of crude oil per year and is involved in the production of jet fuel.

item.title: Oleshky ceasefire will not bring wider truce with Russia, former Ukrainian PM warns
item.description: The first humanitarian operation in years in Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky offers a fragile glimmer of hope for civilians trapped by war, but raises grave concerns over Moscow's true intentions and the fate of those seeking evacuation to Ukrainian-controlled territory.

item.title: What happens to the brain when you eat peanuts daily? New study reveals striking results
item.description: Does eating peanuts every day help to maintain memory as we get older?

item.title: Mexico: world's tallest Catrina unveiled for Día de Muertos in Mexico City
item.description: A 33.4-metre Catrina has broken a Guinness World Record in Mexico City. Towering over the Zócalo, the giant skeleton is surrounded by thousands of marigolds ahead of Day of the Dead celebrations.

item.title: ‘Godspeed, Captain’: Heartfelt tributes pour in for Sir Patrick Stewart
item.description: Tributes have poured in following the death of British actor Patrick Stewart, celebrated for his decades-long Shakespearean stage career and iconic roles in the Star Trek and X-Men franchises.

item.title: DR Congo: MSF celebrates Ebola patient discharges in Ituri province
item.description: Dancing and singing erupted at an Ebola treatment centre in DR Congo as the last patients were discharged. For the first time since May, the MSF-run facility has no confirmed cases under treatment, although the wider outbreak continues.

item.title: ‘A living hell’: The occupied town of Oleshky captures the world’s attention — including Melania Trump’s
item.description: Hello, and happy Friday. My name is Angela Skujins. On today’s agenda: the horrors of a Russian-captured community, EU-Canada affairs throw up more questions than answers, and hefty fines for angry Albanian protesters. Let’s go.

item.title: Netanyahu bloc first but without majority as Arab parties hold balance of power in Israel election
item.description: The result means Israel is now set to face a lengthy and likely tricky period of negotiations as party leaders work to form a government.

item.title: Knot for eating: Welcome to the Italian restaurant where every meal is knitted
item.description: From fluffy tiramisu to puffy ravioli, the food is as delicious as it is deceptive at 'Kate's Knitalian' — an immersive new art exhibition in London.

item.title: Inside Copenhagen’s swanky new ‘water culture house’ with 10 pools, three saunas and an onsen
item.description: Set to open on Paper Island in early December, KAI will have multiple pools, wellness facilities and also offer bathers access to the harbour’s waters for swimming.

item.title: Europe Today: Rare Oleshky truce holds in Ukraine, Albania imposes heavy fines on protesters
item.description: A rare ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky enters its fourth day as aid is expected to arrive, after a Russian drone killed at least 14 at Dnipro's station. In Albania, protesters face fines up to €5,500. We also look at Israel's deadlock and the Ebola epidemic in Congo.

item.title: ‘Historic milestone’ for Greenland as new international airport opens in Ilulissat
item.description: Greenland has completed its three-airport expansion, with Ilulissat’s new international gateway opening up direct access to Disko Bay and North Greenland.

item.title: The new time lord: Wei Koh on his first year as GPHG jury president
item.description: With just a week to go before the prestigious awards at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève, Euronews Culture caught up with one of watchmaking's most charismatic figures, Wei Koh, founder of media company Revolution and, for the first time, jury president of GPHG, the "Oscars of watchmaking".

item.title: 'Why would we want to leave?': Fiji islanders work on climate resilience to avoid relocation
item.description: Residents of Fiji's tiny Serua Island have rejected calls to relocate, instead opting to renovate flimsy coastal homes.

item.title: EU and Canada to seal broader, deeper alliance in Trump's long shadow
item.description: The EU-Canada summit in Montréal will expand cooperation across multiple areas, including trade, investment, supply chains, AI, climate, security and the Arctic, and advance Canada's integration into EU programmes.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 30th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 30th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: These are the world’s 20 most-visited museums – and five are in Europe
item.description: China dominated the list, claiming the number one spot with the Palace Museum in Beijing and having 12 entries in the top 20 overall.

item.title: Bank of Japan says inflation hit 2% target after 13 years
item.description: The Bank of Japan said on Friday inflation had hit its 2% target, more than 13 years after it adopted the goal in a bid to pull the economy out of deflation, but held off hiking interest rates for now.

item.title: The change vote turns: Why America's midterms could punish the party that promised it
item.description: Two years after riding a wave of discontent to total control of Washington, Donald Trump and the Republicans face the same message of change that brought them to power. This time, it's aimed squarely at them.

item.title: More greens, higher testosterone? What a Finnish study found
item.description: Research involving more than 2,500 men found contrasting associations between animal and plant protein intake — but does not show that changing diets boosts testosterone.

item.title: Largest bank heist in history: Binance hack rocks crypto industry
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that hit around $6.3 billion (€5.5bn) in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian strike kills two teenage girls in Chernihiv
item.description: A Russian strike on Chernihiv killed two 15-year-old girls and injured 25 people, local officials say. Meanwhile, a US-brokered ceasefire in southern Ukraine is allowing demining work aimed at opening humanitarian routes.

item.title: Spain: minute of silence for train crash victims as king visits hospital
item.description: Spain is mourning 69 people killed in a high-speed train collision near Toledo. As King Felipe VI visits a hospital treating the injured, rescuers continue searching the wreckage and a minute of silence is held at the crash site.

item.title: The World Judo Tour returns to Abu Dhabi with Day 1 wins
item.description: The Abu Dhabi Grand Slam kicked off with historic gold for Azerbaijan's Konul Aliyeva, another title for Balabay Aghayev and stunning victories from Tihea Topolovec and Sukhrob Boqiev. France's Martha Fawaz also struck gold on an action-packed opening day.
